.github: GitHub's own files: the checks that run on every push, the issue and pull-request forms
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE: The forms for reporting a bug or asking for a feature
.github/workflows: The automatic checks (type check, tests, lint, build, image build) that run on GitHub
dev: Things for the development machine only
dev/testserver: The throwaway Jellyfin test server: its Docker setup (its data is not in the repository)
docs: The project's documents: what was done, decided and changed from the TV app, and this map
docs/spec: How the TV app behaves, written down from its source: what the web port follows
e2e: The browser tests: they drive the real app in real browsers against the test server
e2e/fixtures: What every browser test starts from: sign-in, the app helper, the server helper, the settings
e2e/flows: Longer journeys through the app, played as tests
e2e/specs: The browser tests themselves, one file per area of the app
public: Files served as they are: the icon, the default settings file, the check for browsers that are too old
server: The small production server: serves the built app, its settings, and passes requests on to Seerr
src: The app itself: everything that runs in the browser
src/api: Talking to the servers: the Jellyfin sign-in and session, image addresses, shared data-loading helpers and the Seerr (Discover) connection
src/api/hooks: Small shared data-loading hooks, for example the list of the user's libraries
src/api/playback: Builders for the media addresses the player uses: video streams, trickplay thumbnails, subtitles and attachments
src/api/seerr: Everything for Seerr, the request service behind Discover: connection, sign-in, permissions, requests, search results and filters
src/app: The frame of the app: start-up, routes, the shell around every page, error and loading screens, toasts, and the arrow-key navigation
src/app/dev: A developer-only sign-in page that is only available while running locally, not in the real site
src/app/shell: The sidebar (nav drawer), the clock, the Back button, the backdrop picture, the copy of the page behind Settings, and focus/Back handling
src/features: One folder per area of the app (Home, Settings, the player ...): each screen and the parts only it uses
src/features/browse: Library pages: movie/TV libraries with tabs, plain folders, favourites, genre/studio lists and the 'View more' grid
src/features/browse/components: Parts of library pages: the grid, its header buttons (sort, filter, view options), tabs, list rows and the Recommended tab
src/features/browse/data: What library pages ask the server: grid requests, paging, filter values, saved sort/filter/view state, Recommended rows
src/features/browse/model: Rules for library pages without any screen: sort lists, filters, view options, columns, letter jump, favourite types
src/features/common: Pieces many pages share: item right-click menu, card data, item text, image choice, hover delay, caches and library lists
src/features/detail: The detail pages opened from a card: movie, episode, series, box set, playlist and person, with the pieces they share
src/features/detail/collection: The box-set (collection) page: its header, buttons, rows or grid of items, and its saved view options and sort
src/features/detail/common: Pieces shared by the detail pages: header text, Play buttons, rows, track choosers, media info, playlists dialog
src/features/detail/episode: The single-episode page, reached only for an episode without a series (normal episodes open in the series page)
src/features/detail/movie: The movie page (also used for videos, music videos, recordings and trailers)
src/features/detail/person: The page of an actor or crew member: photo, birth details, biography and their movies, shows and episodes
src/features/detail/playlist: The playlist page: a library-style list of the playlist's items with Move up, Move down and More on each row
src/features/detail/series: The series pages: the series start page, and the season tabs with the episode strip and the focused episode's details
src/features/discover: Seerr: the Discover page and its tabs, movie/series/person pages, request dialogs, and the Seerr sign-in and settings entry
src/features/home: The Home page: its header, its rows of cards, the View more grid, and how Home remembers focus and scroll
src/features/home/data: Loading Home: which server requests each Home row makes, and how the rows are fetched and kept fresh
src/features/home/model: The data shape of Home rows: row types, display presets, and where the saved row list comes from (device, server, plugin)
src/features/home/settings: The Customize home page screens: row list, add row, row options, presets, source, global settings, preview and its dialogs
src/features/livetv: Live TV: the Live TV page with its Guide, DVR Schedule and recording-folder tabs, the channel and program cells, and the recording dialogs
src/features/music: Music: album, artist, song and genre pages, the music library tabs, the Now Playing screen, the bottom mini player and the audio engine
src/features/music/components: Small shared music pieces: the album/artist header, the Play/Shuffle button strip, song rows, the playing marker and card rows
src/features/music/data: Where the music pages get their data from the server: item, lyrics and backdrop queries and the song lists a queue is filled from
src/features/music/library: The music library page's own pieces: its five tabs, the Recommended tab's rows and the artist list requests
src/features/music/menu: The right-click / three-dot menus of songs, albums, artists and queue rows on the music pages
src/features/music/nowplaying: The parts of the Now Playing screen: seek bar, queue list, lyrics, bar visualizer, view options and the changing backdrop
src/features/music/queue: The pure rules of the play queue: ordering, shuffle, repeat, moving and removing entries
src/features/music/service: The music engine: the audio element, play/pause/next, stream address, progress reports to the server and the visualizer tap
src/features/photos: Photos: photo albums and libraries as a grid, the full-screen photo viewer and slideshow, the image filter, and the idle screensaver
src/features/playback: The player page: the video screen with its overlay, keys, pointer and touch handling, and the error screen
src/features/playback/engine: The player's brain with no screen of its own: loads the stream, picks tracks, reports progress, draws subtitles on the video
src/features/playback/engine/__dev: A developer-only test page for the player engine, opened with ?debug=1 in dev builds; not in the real app
src/features/playback/engine/subtitles: Subtitle files: fetching and reading them, reading direction (Hebrew, Arabic) and the style settings turned into CSS
src/features/playback/ui: Everything drawn over the video: control strip, buttons, seek bar, menus and sheets, skip, next up, debug panel, and the keys
src/features/search: The Search page: search bar, voice search, result rows or one combined grid, the Discover results and the search options
src/features/settings: Everything in Settings: the panel and its rows, the dialogs they open, the subtitle style editor, and the Debug and License pages
src/features/settings/assets: The sample picture (eclipse.jpeg) shown behind the example subtitles in the subtitle style editor
src/features/setup: Everything before Home: the server picker, the user picker, the sign-in dialog, Quick Connect and the PIN screens
src/i18n: Languages: loading the chosen language, right-to-left handling and the text of every label in the app
src/i18n/extra: The English texts that the Android app does not have and that the web version added (keys starting with web_)
src/i18n/locales: One file of translated texts per language, plus the list of available languages; generated from the Android app
src/lib: Small plain helpers with no screen of their own: time and number formatting, ids, browser storage and server-version checks
src/stores: What the app remembers: the saved preferences, the signed-in servers and users, remembered audio/subtitle choices and the music queue
src/theme: The look of the whole app: theme colours, text sizes, the interface scale and the global base styles
src/theme/fonts: The icon font (Font Awesome solid) used for the small icons in the sidebar and elsewhere
src/ui: The shared parts every screen is built from: buttons, cards, rows, dialogs, menus, inputs, icons, spinners and helpers
src/ui/assets: The app logo pictures (the cube icon and the banner with the name) used by the logo component
src/ui/buttons: The pill buttons: normal, text, round icon, the Play-style button that opens to show its label, and the detail-page button row
src/ui/cards: Every card (poster, wide, grid, person, genre, chapter, server and user circles) plus their badges, pills and progress bar
src/ui/feedback: Spinners, the loading page, the error message block and the small toast pop-up messages
src/ui/gallery: A developer-only page (/dev/gallery) that shows every shared part side by side, with made-up pictures
src/ui/icons: The icon sets: Material icons, Font Awesome glyphs, the app's own drawn icons and the app logo
src/ui/inputs: Text boxes, the search box, the slider and the on/off switches
src/ui/lib: Behind-the-scenes helpers: focus and keyboard rules, mouse/touch scrolling, menu positions, text scrolling, colours from ids
src/ui/overlays: Pop-ups: the dialog shell, option lists, right-click menus, drop-down menus, confirm dialogs and the list rows inside them
src/ui/rows: Horizontal card rows with arrows, the scrolling card grid, the A-Z letter strip and the row loading placeholder
src/ui/text: Text pieces: scrolling titles, overview text, rating stars, quick-details line, stream chips, the tab strip and logo-or-title
tools: Scripts for building and checking the project (generators, the screenshot crawler, the test server setup)
tools/code-map: The hand-kept lists behind docs/CODE-MAP.md: what you see and where it is, one line per folder
tools/refshots: Takes the reference pictures of the Android TV app in an emulator
tools/shots: The screenshot crawler: photographs every screen of the web app and compares with the TV pictures
tools/testserver: Sets up the throwaway test server and generates its small test films and series
types: Type descriptions for libraries that ship none
vendor: Third-party code kept in the repository
vendor/rvfc-polyfill: A stand-in for a browser feature (video frame callbacks) that the ASS subtitle renderer needs
